title: Veridian Payments integration playbook (draft)
content:
Context: quick running notes from discovery and technical sync with Veridian Payments (call 2025-11-01). Customer wants to augment their fraud scoring pipeline with an LLM for anomaly explanations + short-term memory for customer history retrieval. They are constrained by PCI requirements and strict latency targets for pre-authorization scoring (<= 120ms p95). This doc is a working playbook — keep light, actionable, and focused on next steps for SE + infra + product small team.

Participants:
- Veridian: Lina Okoro (Eng lead), Ravi Kumar (Security), Maya Holt (Product)
- Redwood: Priya Raghunathan (SE), Diego Marquez (Infra), Samir Patel (APPLIED ML)

High-level ask from Veridian:
- Real-time explainability snippets for transactions flagged by rule engine (human readable reasons)
- Similarity search over last 90 days of customer transactions (embeddings) for context
- Must run inside their VPC / on-prem (no external data exfiltration) for PCI scope reduction
- Latency SLO: 120ms p95 for scoring path (end-to-end addition cannot exceed this)
- Audit/logging retention: 24 months with tamper-evident logs

Key constraints / gotchas discussed:
- PCI and PII: They require tokenization and strict redaction pre-send. We must verify where tokenization happens — ideally on their side before hitting the Redwood Private control plane. Confirm whether Redwood Private will accept already-tokenized payloads or whether they want us to host a tokenization adapter inside their VPC.
- Cold KV cache blowups: If we do prefix caching for customer conversation/history, cold-starts can spike GPU work. Design: warm cache with scheduled background prefetch for top X high-risk customers (Veridian has daily list of ~300K users; need sampling strategy).
- Quantized model accuracy: Customer is worried about hallucinations in explainability. Recommend initial use of fp16 / bfloat16 on H100s for the explanation model, fallback to quantized smaller model for degraded mode. Need empirical eval against their labeled fraud explanations set.
- Embeddings scale: 90 days * 100M txns -> embeddings store grows fast. Discussed semantic dedupe and retention policy (retain only top-K per account or rolling window). Also considered approximate nearest neighbors hosted in their VPC vs managed vector store.
- TLS + mTLS: Veridian requires mutual TLS for control-plane + data-plane. Confirm Redwood Private supports mTLS termination in-customer VPC. Also confirm KMS integration: customer uses AWS CloudHSM — need a plan for HSM-backed keys and key rotation.
- Model pinning and rollouts: They will want pinned versions for auditability. Must show step-by-step rollback and canary policies in the Private control plane.

Technical proposals (draft):
1) Architecture variant A (recommended initial):
   - Redwood Private deployed in Veridian VPC (control plane local).
   - Tokenization + PII redaction adapter runs as sidecar in ingress subnet (customer-maintained).
   - Explanation model: medium-sized causal model (Llama2-13B-ish equivalent) on H100 fp16 with batching disabled for explanation path (prefer micro-batching or streaming to meet latency).
   - Embeddings: offline pipeline writes 1536-d embeddings to an in-VPC vector DB (FAISS on k8s or Milvus); Redwood provides SDK + batch encoder job (nightly + near-realtime via incremental workers).
   - Fallback: lightweight distilled model (quantized) for times when GPU capacity is saturated; requests flagged for fallback logged for quality monitoring.

2) Architecture variant B (if infra budget tight):
   - Hosted Redwood API for non-PII paths (explainability examples stripped) + Private-only for all tokens flagged as PCI. Not ideal but reduces infra footprint.

Performance notes / estimates (very rough):
- Explanation model: ~40-70ms per request on H100 for short prompts if we avoid long context and disable heavy generation (we expect 16-48 token answers). Need bench with their prompt templates.
- Embedding throughput: batch encoder can do ~20K embeddings/minute per A100 depending on batch size and seq len; verify against their nightly load.
- Network hops: mTLS handshake overhead ~20ms on cold connections — recommend connection pooling and keep-alive in the SDK.

Open questions (to clarify with Veridian):
- Exact size and distribution of tokenized payloads (typical seq len) for explanation prompt templates.
- Do they require explanations to be stored as part of the audit trail, or only the model inputs/outputs hashes? GDPR/PCI may differ.
- Which accounts must be in-scope for 90-day embeddings retention? All accounts or high-risk cohorts only?
- SLA expectations for model retraining / label feedback loop (they want "explainability accuracy" to improve over time).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Diego: prototype mTLS termination doc + config snippet for Redwood Private in-customer VPC (ETA 2025-11-10)
- Priya: collect 5 example prompt templates from Veridian for bench (ETA 2025-11-05) -> Lina to send
- Samir: run 3 model evals (13B fp16, 7B q4_0, distilled 3B) against Veridian's sample explanations and report delta in hallucination rate (ETA 2025-11-18)
- Diego + Samir: cost/throughput estimation spreadsheet for H100 vs A100 options (ETA 2025-11-12)
- Priya: draft security checklist for PCI scoping (retention, redaction, KMS integration) and share with Veridian security (ETA 2025-11-07)
- Lina (Veridian): share anonymized sample payloads (with redaction) and the list of high-risk accounts for warm cache pilot (ETA 2025-11-06)

Notes-to-self / heuristics: 
- When we talk about embeddings retention, push for rolling top-K per account instead of raw time-window to limit vector DB size.
- Measure regression risk when moving from fp16->quantized; consider hybrid route: emb encoder quantized but explanation model kept in fp16.
- Audit logs: propose cryptographic hash + append-only storage (S3 with Object Lock) for 24-month tamper-evident requirement.

Misc snippets from call (verbatim bits):
- Lina: "If we can keep the model inside our VPC and not send PHI/PII anywhere, legal will be happy — but latency is non-negotiable."
- Ravi: "We want to be able to prove what model version produced each explanation — that will be part of compliance audits."

Next meeting: 2025-11-12 technical deep-dive (model prompt bench + infra sizing). Prep list: Diego to bring mTLS diagram; Samir to bring preliminary eval numbers; Priya to bring sample prompts + a short recommended fallback policy doc.

Unresolved follow-ups to add to JIRA:
- JIRA-5902: mTLS + KMS checklist for Veridian Private deployment
- JIRA-5903: Benchmark explanation models on Veridian prompts (dataset from Lina)
- JIRA-5904: Embeddings retention policy proposal + cost estimates

Summary verdict (for now): Customer is a good fit for Redwood Private but they will need a small, careful pilot (warm-cache + limited cohort) to validate latency and accuracy tradeoffs. Focus pilot on high-risk accounts to limit vector DB cost and to collect eval signal.

End of notes. Marking as draft — will convert to playbook and hand off to onboarding once benchmarks validate the suggested stack.
